messages.decoding: Etherscan txlist input data decoded as UTF-8 (0xaa byte = newline); one message needed a first-nibble shift. Covers txs of the EOA and txs sent to Yoink bot contracts. Blockscan Chat messages are off-chain and not included.

groups.heading: SushiSwap, April 2023
groups.context: A message signed as Sushi's security contact reached Yoink's wallet about five hours after the first RouteProcessor2 copy; Yoink answered the next day. That reply reverted, so the 380 ETH it carries did not move in this transaction. A repeat that did move 380 ETH to the multisig named in the first message landed about three and a half minutes later.

messages.text:
Funds from ongoing sushiswap routeprocoessor2.sol hack were sent to your address. We would like you to return the funds to Sushiswap Multisig Ops - 0x19B3Eb3Af5D93b77a5619b047De0EED7115A19e7
We thank you for the whitehack.
contact - [contact redacted]
Normally would ask for a 10% bounty for intercepting a blackhat, but seems this was just a dumbhat. Also, NotYoink, stop bribing so much!

extra.label: The repeat transfer of 380 ETH that succeeded

groups.heading: Conic Finance, July 2023
groups.context: Not one of the races counted here. It shows how a return gets negotiated, arithmetic included.

messages.text: This is a message from Conic Finance. Your bot has replicated an attack on Conic Finance that resulted in funds being stolen. We are writing you to know if you would be open to returning these funds in exchange for a bounty.

By my calculations, my bot took 125.82415 Eth while spending 35.48275 in gas fees and bribes, leaving 90.34139 to return. Does that seem correct? Would appreciate a bounty, but leave that up to you. Let me know how much / where to return the funds.

Thank you very much for the quick reply and for accepting to return the funds. This is very much appreciated in these hard times for us. These are also the numbers we computed. We would like to offer you a bounty of 10% of your profits, so could you please return 81.307251 ETH to this address (conicfinance.eth)? We will then proceed to reimburse the LPs who lost funds in the process. You can double-check that this is indeed the address that deployed the Conic crvUSD pool (0x369cbc5c6f139b1132d3b91b87241b37fc5b971f) that was drained in the incident. Thank you again for your cooperation.

groups.heading: Paraswap, March 2024
groups.context: Paraswap asked for the money back. The two sides disagree about whether the payment to the validator at the end of the block counts against Yoink's profit.

messages.text: Were there any other txs from me other than 0x35a7? If not, then I've already repaid my entire profit (plus some extra from a following arbitrage!) Note the validator payment at the end of the block which limits the funds I'm able to return.
Thanks for your cooperation and good faith. 0x35a7 took 12,479 OPSEC from the user, which is 6.46 ETH instead of 4.342 ETH that you sent back. Could you please send the rest? Thanks for your help!

Believe I've explained this already, but lets try one more time. I've already sent you more than 100% of my profits from 0x35a7. Yes the token was sold for 6.45 Eth, but in order to land this tx, I had to pay 2.22 Eth to the validator in a tx at the end of the block. You are, or course, welcome to try and recover the remaining amount from the validator.

groups.heading: Ronin bridge, August 2024

messages.text: Hey, thanks a lot for white hat saving user funds today. Can we chat over Blockscan chat?
